hello.note: The everyday Brazilian hello, fine with almost anyone: Oi.

goodbye.note: More formal: Até logo. Adeus sounds final, like a farewell for good.

thank_you.note: A woman says: Obrigada. Very casual: Valeu!

youre_welcome.note: Also common: Por nada, or Imagina!

yes.note: Brazilians often answer by repeating the verb instead: Você quer? — Quero.

no.note: The ão is nasal: like 'now' said through the nose.

sorry.note: Very common in speech: Desculpa. For deep regret or condolences: Sinto muito.

excuse_me.note: Also used to get past someone. To call a waiter: Por favor! or Moço! (to a woman: Moça!)

good_morning.note: Used until about noon; after that: Boa tarde.

how_are_you.note: Very common and still polite: Tudo bem? The usual reply: Tudo, e você?

im_fine.note: A woman says: Estou bem, obrigada. In casual speech: Tô bem.

whats_your_name.note: Also common: Como você se chama?

nice_to_meet_you.note: Often just: Prazer! Reply: O prazer é meu.

where_from.note: To an older person: De onde o senhor é? (to a woman: a senhora)

im_from.note: De merges with the country's article: do Brasil, da Itália, dos Estados Unidos; but de Portugal.

speak_english.note: More formal: O senhor fala inglês? (to a woman: A senhora)

dont_understand.note: Brazilians use this past form in conversation. For a language in general: Não entendo.

speak_slowly.text: Pode falar mais devagar, por favor?
speak_slowly.note: Asking with pode (can you) is the polite way; Fale mais devagar sounds like an order.

where.note: Where to?: Para onde? (in speech: Pra onde?)

what.note: To ask someone to repeat, more politely: Como?

why.note: Two words with an accent here; the answer 'because' is one word: porque.

who.note: Sounds like 'kayn' said through the nose; the final m itself isn't pronounced.

where_bathroom.note: Banheiro is the Brazilian word; in Portugal: casa de banho.

can_you_help.note: Brazilians put me before the verb; Portugal says ajudar-me. Add por favor to soften it.

what_means.note: Also common: O que quer dizer isso?

one.note: Before a feminine noun: uma (uma cerveja). It also means 'a/an'.

two.note: Before a feminine noun: duas (duas horas).

six.note: Reading out phone numbers, Brazilians say meia (half a dozen) so it isn't confused with três.

water.note: Still: água sem gás. Sparkling: água com gás.

coffee.note: A small black coffee is a cafezinho; with milk: café com leite.

bread.note: Nasal ão, as in não. The classic breakfast roll: pão francês.

im_hungry.note: Built with estar com + noun, like Estou com sede (thirsty). In speech: Tô com fome.

menu_please.note: Cardápio is Brazilian; in Portugal: a ementa. Menu is also understood.

bill_please.note: Also common: Pode fechar a conta, por favor?

delicious.note: Also: Está delicioso! In speech: Tá uma delícia!

no_meat.note: Or: Sou vegetariano (a woman: Sou vegetariana).

left.note: On/to the left: à esquerda. Turn left: Vire à esquerda.

right.note: On/to the right: à direita. Don't confuse with direto (straight on).

straight_ahead.note: Also common in Brazil: reto or direto (Siga reto).

stop_here.note: Asking with pode is politer than the bare command Pare aqui.

hotel.note: The h is silent and the final l sounds like w: oh-TEHW (open e, as in 'bet').

train_station.note: In Portugal: estação de comboios. Subway station: estação de metrô.

want_to_go.note: Softer: Queria ir para … In speech para often becomes pra.

is_it_far.note: Also: Fica longe? The opposite is perto (near).

one_ticket.note: For a trip: passagem. Metro or city ticket: bilhete. Show or match: ingresso.

too_expensive.note: In speech: Tá muito caro. Also: Está caro demais.

cheaper.note: Brazilians use tem for 'do you have / is there'. Also: Tem alguma coisa mais barata?

id_like_this.note: Queria is the polite 'I'd like'. When buying: Vou levar esse (I'll take this one).

just_looking.note: Also: Só estou olhando. In speech: Tô só dando uma olhada.

pay_card.note: You may be asked: Crédito ou débito? Brazilians also pay by Pix, an instant bank transfer.

cash.note: Dinheiro alone means money in general. To pay in cash: pagar em dinheiro.

small.note: Feminine: pequena. Clothing sizes: P, M, G (pequeno, médio, grande).

tomorrow.note: Don't mix it up with de manhã (in the morning). Tomorrow morning: amanhã de manhã.

good_evening.note: Said once it's dark; the same words also mean good night. Before that, in the afternoon: Boa tarde.

good_night.note: The same words as good evening. Before bed you may add: Durma bem.

see_you_later.note: Also: Até logo. See you tomorrow: Até amanhã.

wait_moment.note: Casual: Peraí! (from espera aí) or Só um minutinho.

every_day.note: Also: todos os dias. All day long is o dia todo.

call_police.note: To one person: Chame a polícia! Police in Brazil: dial 190.

need_doctor.note: Urgently, to people around you: Chamem um médico!

im_lost.note: A woman says: Estou perdida. In speech: Tô perdido.

dont_feel_well.note: Also very common: Estou passando mal.

hospital.note: The h is silent and the final l sounds like w: os-pee-TOW, rhyming with 'now'.

lost_phone.note: Celular is the Brazilian word; in Portugal: telemóvel.

allergic.note: A woman says: Sou alérgica a … For anyone: Tenho alergia a …

no_problem.note: Very Brazilian alternatives: Tranquilo! or Beleza!

of_course.note: Stronger: Claro que sim! or Com certeza!

dont_know.note: Casual, a bit dismissive: Sei lá.

i_like_it.note: Past form, used when reacting to something you've just seen or tried. Liking it in general: Eu gosto.

dont_like_it.note: About something you've just tried. In general: Não gosto.

im_tired.note: A woman says: Estou cansada. In speech: Tô cansado.

im_happy.note: Same for men and women. Also: Estou contente.

welcome.note: To a woman: Seja bem-vinda! To a group: Sejam bem-vindos!

congratulations.note: Also what you say for 'happy birthday'.
